findings.evidence:
## When to use

When a run, a review or an execution step calls an external AI CLI and acts on the result.
findings.fix: Move this trigger into the description (already covered there) and delete the body section, recording the removal: the body is invisible until the skill has already triggered.

findings.evidence:
## What a skill does on a stop

The caller rules live in [`../SKILL.md`](../SKILL.md), sections 6, 7 and 8. In short: print the `cross-ai: report` and `AIKIT-XAI` lines verbatim...
findings.fix: Delete this restatement of SKILL.md sections 6-8 and keep only the pointer, recording the removal; the caller rules already live in the skill body.

findings.evidence: The skill is a Tool-pattern decision catalog (exit table, setting reasons, findings) but sections 2, 3 and 6 are dense paragraphs an agent must re-parse to act.
findings.fix: Keep the Tool pattern. Split the launch, wait and hard-tier paragraphs into the same numbered decision steps the exit and findings tables already use, leaving the exact commands and stop rules in place.

findings.evidence: ## Pitfalls lists specific NEVER facts, but several items (process table shows the prompt, two timeouts, atomic rewrites keep the mode) have no why.
findings.fix: Add one clause of why to each Pitfalls bullet that lacks it, for example that a prompt on argv is visible to other users via the process table, and that a hand replacement of a config file can drop its mode and break the next confined read.

findings.evidence: MANDATORY before the first launch on a host: read references/launch-and-wait.md for that host's background or foreground pattern.
findings.fix: Gate the read by host: read references/launch-and-wait.md only for the host you are running in, and do not load the other hosts' sections. The quota policy is already correctly gated to config, overlay and route= work.

findings.evidence: Where Claude Code's CronCreate is callable, schedule one one-shot job at retry_after_s. It fires on whole minutes: pick the first whole minute at or after retry_after_s that is not :00 or :30.
findings.fix: Give the exact cron field order and one worked example (retry_after_s=300 at 10:07 becomes minute 12) so the one-shot cannot be built two ways; keep the print-and-stop handoff when next run cannot be confirmed.

findings.evidence: 16 queries (8 should-trigger, 8 should-not-trigger), short of about 20 with 8-10 each side; negatives include near-misses (reviewer setup, GSD config, session wake).
findings.fix: Add two should-trigger and two should-not-trigger queries with realistic context, including one near-miss that mentions a CLI or a 429 but asks for reviewer setup or a usage dashboard rather than a lane action.

findings.evidence: Ten evals have realistic prompts, expected output and verifiable assertions, but only two supply input files and several outcomes (herdr off, locked, crash, reset time) are graded from prose with no lane.err fixture.
findings.fix: Add lane.err fixtures under evals/files/ for the locked, crash and stated-reset cases, and point those evals' files arrays at them so the assertions can be checked against a real status line.

findings.evidence: Every other non-zero exit (a bare 75, any 69 including stopped=hard-waits or stopped=cap, 1, 2, 124, 127) gets the section 6 notice and the answer abort.
findings.fix: Name the section 6 notice as the hard-waits/cap verbatim report only, and say a bare 75, exit 1, 2, 124 or 127 gets the section 4 report instead; stopped=hard-waits and stopped=cap are exit 69, which the same sentence already covers.

findings.evidence: On an exit 75 with retry_after_s=, schedule one one-shot CronCreate at retry_after_s and re-invoke the same lane, per section 6.
findings.fix: Restate the :00/:30 shift and the confirm-next-run gate in this Claude Code section, or say to apply section 6's minute rule before scheduling, so this file cannot be followed into an early fire.
